about: Attorney Roger W. Stelk founded his Arlington Heights law firm, the Law Office of Roger W. Stelk, in 1995. Over the past 35-plus years, Mr. Stelk has earned a reputation as one of the Chicago area's leading family law attorneys. It is the combination of his excellent reputation and his long record of success that leads clients from throughout northeastern Illinois to his firm for assistance with a variety of family law matters, including:

• Divorce, including high-asset divorce • Property and debt division • Spousal maintenance • Child support • Child custody and visitation • Paternity • Parental relocations • Post-decree modifications

Mr. Stelk began his legal career in 1987 after earning his law degree from The John Marshall Law School (now University of Illinois Chicago School of Law) and his approval to practice law in the state of Illinois. Prior to founding his own firm, Mr. Stelk gained valuable experience as an associate at Chicago-area firms. Since founding his firm, he has served as an arbitrator for Lake and Cook counties and as a court facilitator for Cook County.

Over the course of Mr. Stelk's long career, he has not only built an outstanding reputation, but he has also earned the respect of both his clients and his peers. He has a "Superb" Avvo rating, and he is a recipient of Avvo's Clients' Choice award. In addition, he has received an AV Preeminent peer review rating* from Martindale-Hubbell.

Attorney Stelk is the author of a number of legal guides and an active member of the legal community. He is a member of the Illinois State Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the McHenry County Bar Association, the Chicago Bar Association and the Northwest Suburban Bar Association.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.
